Ashwin (eng-runtime): Quick heads-up — I ran a sequence-length sweep on the hybrid replay+synth harness this morning. Dataset: mix of 60% short (32), 30% mid (512), 10% long (8192) but with prefill-heavy load (prefill tokens ~70% of total). Root run id: seqlen-sweep-0301. Observed two odd regression cases where kernel-autoselect chose the q8_matmul path for long-prefill and latency p95 jumped ~18% vs the fixed fp16 kernel baseline.

Maria (eng-ml): Can you paste the harness config and the exact numbers? Also which model variant and quant config?

Ashwin (eng-runtime): Sure — harness command and stripped config below:

```
./harness/run_bench --replay=customer_dump_2025-10 --synth-weight=0.4 --seqlen-mix=60,30,10 --prefill-mode=dominant --kernel-autoselect=on --quant-mode=q8_02
```

seeds: model=redwood-7b-v1, kv_cache=true, batcher=dynamic-timeout(10ms)

Summary CSV (aggregate across 30m run):
median_tokens_s, p95_latency_ms, kv_hit_ratio, kernel_choice_majority
12400, 84, 0.71, fp16_matmul
11800, 99, 0.70, q8_matmul
12150, 87, 0.72, mixed

Explanation: first line = baseline (forced fp16), second = kernel-autoselect case where q8 dominated for long prefill windows, third = mixed run where we forced a 50/50 route policy.

Leo (perf): That +18% at p95 is scary but median looks similar. Do you have breakdown by phase (prefill vs decode)?

Ashwin (eng-runtime): Yes — phase split below (p95 latency in ms):
prefill_p95, decode_p95
162, 42  <-- q8_autoselect run
138, 40  <-- fp16_forced baseline

So most regression is prefill-heavy. Profiling shows longer matmul scheduling stalls when q8 path used with long KV loads. Attached sample perf trace excerpt: CPU wait on copy_to_device up ~2.4x during prefill windows.

Sam (benchmarking): Can you post the kernel selection counts? I want to see at what sequence length the selector flips.

Ashwin (eng-runtime): Selector histogram (per request):
<=256: fp16 86%, q8 14%
257-1024: fp16 52%, q8 48%
>1024: q8 84%, fp16 16%

So it decisively flips for >1k lengths. But in prefill-dominant workload many requests have a prefill ~8k then decode short, so the selector chooses q8 early and keeps path which interacts badly with KV cache streaming.

Maria (eng-ml): Did you check batcher behavior? Continuous batching + large prefill can increase inter-token gap and change kernel perf. Any batching stats?

Ashwin (eng-runtime): Batcher summary (dynamic-timeout 10ms):
avg_batch_size_prefill = 4.2 tokens/request; avg_batch_latency = 12ms; batcher_queue_time spikes during long prefill windows (tail up to 45ms). When q8 selected, effective per-token compute is slightly faster, but the GPU kernel launch overhead + extra memcpy for q8 path kills p95 when batch sizes are small and KV cache copy patterns are heavy.

perf-bot: benchmark seqlen-sweep-0301 completed. artifacts: s3://perf/seqlen-sweep-0301/{profiles,metrics.csv,heatmaps}.

Leo (perf): Good to have artifacts. Proposal: re-run with two targeted experiments — 1) force kernel to fp16 for >1k sequences to check if we can avoid regression, 2) keep autoselect but switch batcher policy to 'max-fill(16, timeout=4ms)' to increase avg batch size and reduce launch overhead. Thoughts?

Ashwin (eng-runtime): Agreed. I already kicked off both jobs. Preliminary warm-up shows forcing fp16 for >1k removes the p95 regression (prefill_p95 down to 140ms). The max-fill tweak reduced p95 by ~6% on autoselect case (so still worse than forced fp16). Full re-run expected in 40m.

Maria (eng-ml): We should also run apples-to-apples (same token count, same routing) between replay-only and synth-only to ensure the behaviour isn't dataset-specific. Could be replay generator has longer contiguous KV patterns.

Sam (benchmarking): Agreed — I'll schedule replay-only / synth-only runs with identical seed and exactly-matched token volume. Also will add the KV-copy microbenchmark (single-request prefill=8192, measure copy_to_device time distribution).

Ashwin (eng-runtime): Next steps: 1) collect kernel-level traces for the autoselect path (nvprof + our kernel-metrics), 2) test selector heuristics: add a prefill-aware penalty so long-prefill requests bias toward fp16, 3) evaluate batcher max-fill policy impact across different traffic mixes. I'll post results when 40m sweep completes.

Leo (perf): If the prefill-aware selector fix looks noisy, consider a cheap fallback: detect long-prefill and prefer kernel with fewer memcpy stages. Should be small change.

Ashwin (eng-runtime): Noted. If anyone wants early access to artifacts, ping me and I'll share S3 links. Also flagging as potential perf regression ticket if autoselect remains default for production.

Maria (eng-ml): Thanks — this is actionable. Ping when the 2nd run finishes.

Ashwin (eng-runtime): Will do.

perf-bot: re-run seqlen-sweep-0301-2 started (forced-fp16>1k).
